thesis: The memory supercycle made visible: revenue up ~300% YoY to $41.5B, a $50B next-quarter guide, and HBM effectively sold out on ~$100B of binding multi-year contracts — but memory is the highest-beta seat in the sector, so size it like the cyclical it remains.
markdown:
## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
**BUY** with $1,350 price target (+17.9% from $1,145.28, as of early July 2026) over 12 months. Micron is the purest listed expression of the AI memory supercycle: fiscal Q3 2026 (reported June 24) revenue rose more than 300% YoY to a record $41.46B, Q4 guidance of ~$50B smashed the $43.6B consensus, and ~$100B of binding multi-year AI memory contracts have effectively sold out HBM supply through 2026. The stock is up ~70% YTD and +211% over 90 days, yet street targets ($1,264 to $1,486 across aggregators) still sit above spot on contract-backed earnings visibility. We are buyers with a cyclical's position size — memory upcycles end abruptly, and this one is priced for continuation.

## FUNDAMENTAL ANALYSIS
**Recent Financial Metrics**: FQ3 2026 (reported 6/24/26): record revenue $41.46B, up more than 300% YoY. Cloud memory revenue $13.77B; core data-center sales up more than sevenfold to $11.5B. FQ4 guidance ~$50B vs ~$43.58B street. Contract backlog: ~$100B of binding multi-year AI memory agreements.

**Industry supply/demand**: Suppliers are prioritizing HBM for AI servers, tightening conventional DRAM and lifting prices across the complex; BofA sizes the 2026 HBM market at $54.6B (+58% YoY). DRAM industry capex is rising 14% to ~$61B — still disciplined relative to demand growth, which is what keeps pricing firm.

**Peer Comparison**: Against SK hynix and Samsung, Micron's advantage this cycle is contract structure (binding multi-year take-or-pay-style agreements) and US-domiciled supply for US hyperscalers. The whole oligopoly is sold out; share shifts matter less than pricing discipline holding.

**Forward Outlook**: Analysts model ~50% revenue growth and ~100% earnings growth for calendar 2026, with earnings visibility extending through the contract book — historically unheard-of for a memory company.

## CATALYST ANALYSIS
**Near-term (0–6 months)**: FQ4 print (~late September) against the $50B guide; HBM4 qualification/ramp milestones; DRAM contract price resets; any new binding AI-lab supply agreements (the recent Anthropic-linked deal coverage shows the demand class broadening beyond hyperscalers).
**Medium-term (6–24 months)**: 2027 HBM supply agreements and pricing; conventional DRAM tightness as HBM cannibalizes wafer capacity; margin trajectory toward cycle highs.
**Event-driven**: Competitor capacity announcements (the cycle-killer to monitor); export-control shifts; litigation headlines (a new lawsuit was in the July news flow — monitor, immaterial to thesis so far).

## VALUATION & PRICE TARGETS
Street targets have been lifted sharply and now span aggregators: ~$1,264 (public.com consensus), ~$1,458 (Simply Wall St), ~$1,486 (Wall Street average per TIKR). LIQD base case $1,350 assumes the $50B guide is met and pricing holds through mid-2027. Bull case $1,700 if HBM pricing extends into 2027 contracts at current escalators. Bear case $700 — deliberately harsh — reflects what memory equities do when supply catches demand (historical downcycles halve these stocks). Probability weighting: 25%/50%/25%.

## RISK ASSESSMENT
**Company risks**: Execution on HBM4 ramp; capacity-expansion discipline; customer concentration in a handful of AI buyers; litigation noise.
**Macro risks**: This is the highest-beta seat at the AI table — a 2027 hyperscaler capex digestion hits memory pricing first and hardest; competitor supply response (SK hynix/Samsung capex) is the classic cycle-ender.
**Position sizing**: 1–3% only. After +211% in 90 days, stage entries; this is a cyclical wearing a growth multiple.

## TECHNICAL CONTEXT & OPTIONS INTELLIGENCE
$1,145.28 after trading as high as ~$1,152 on July 1; coverage notes a ~22% pullback from the highs earlier in July — consistent with a parabolic advance digesting. The 90-day +211% move means the nearest meaningful support sits far below spot; volatility is a feature of the position, not a flaw. Options flow data not sourced in this run — n/a.

## MARKET POSITIONING
Memory is the market's favorite 2026 trade — MU is a top-five holding in SOXX (+91.7% YTD) and the momentum complex owns it. That crowding is why conviction is Medium despite High thesis confidence: the marginal buyer is a momentum fund, and the exit will be crowded too. Within the LIQD Semiconductors framework, MU is the memory allocation alongside the NVDA core (see SEMIS sector note, 7/13/26).
